newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor up on profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Accor up on profit forecast.

text.p: Shares in hotel group Acccor SA rose strongly in a rising market on Thursday on the back of the company's bullish statements at its general meeting on Wednesday.
Dealers also said the share was boosted by reports in French newspapers that influential fund manager George Soros had a 2.18 percent stake in Accor.
At 0851 GMT, Accor was up 2.26 percent at 858 francs. The CAC 40 index at 0909 GMT was up 2.08 pct at 2690.18.
Accor said on Wednesday that the merger of Sphere International, which groups the budget hotels, into Accor would lead to a two franc earnings per share increase from 1997.

Accor chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux said he expected the budget hotel activities, the Ibis, Etap Hotel and Formule 1 chains grouped in the Sphere International division, to generate pre-exceptional profit of 300 million francs this year, up 25 percent.
He told the meeting that the profit objective for Europcar, the 50-50 venture between Accor and Volkswagen, was 50 million francs for 1997.

He said he expected gross operating profit of $40 million a year in 1997-98 for Carlson-Wagonlit Travel, despite the negative $30 million impact of a "re-engineering", and pre-tax, pre-exceptional attributable profit for Carlson-Wagonlit close to that of 1996.
